text:
mara (release-engineer): FYI started the staged rollout of sdk-client 3.0 -> servers at 22:14 UTC. Canary cluster started showing elevated 503s and a wave of cursor errors for paged/streaming responses. Noting here before paging this up.
incident-bot: [ALERT] deploy/sdks/sdk-client:3.0 canary error-rate 12% (threshold 5%) at 22:16:08 UTC. Triggering incident channel.
jin (oncall-sre): seeing errors: `cursor_protocol: version_mismatch` in the canary logs. Grab logs now.
mara: stack trace snippet from canary logs pasted below.
```
ERROR 22:16:05 request_id=abcd1234 cursor_handler.go:87 cursor_version mismatch: expected 2 got 3
WARN 22:16:06 connection=stream-42 client=mobile-sdk timeout waiting for frame
503 22:16:07 proxy=ingress-5 backend=serve-canary status=503
```
paul (release-lead): @mara did we change the cursor wire version in the client build? We had the server-side compatibility flag on.
mara (release-engineer): yes, client 3.0 flips cursor wire v3 by default. We relied on server opt-in that was supposed to land with the template rollout, but looks like some canaries hit a mix of older proxies that don't understand v3.
sophie (customer-ops): any customer-facing impact yet? hit counts?
jin (oncall-sre): short window so far but ~150 failing requests/min across canary nodes, a handful of customer sessions observed streaming disconnects. Gravity: medium. Customer-ops, prepping a note: "some streaming/paging calls may return 503 or cursor errors; retrying should help."
devops-bot: monitoring alert group created: alerts/3114002468-canary-cursor-mismatch. Paging agent: throttle suggestions set to conservative.
paul (release-lead): we need to stop the rollout and kill the feature flag immediately. Mara can you toggle the flag and/or rollback the canary?
mara (release-engineer): doing ff kill now. Command: `feature-flagctl set new_cursor_protocol false --scope=canary`
mara (release-engineer): ff kill applied at 22:18:11 UTC. Pushing a small canary rollback to known-good client 2.9 on affected canary nodes. Running:
```
kubectl -n canary rollout undo deploy/sdk-client-canary --to-revision=rev-20230401
```
22:18:40 kubectl: rollout undo started.
jin (oncall-sre): verifying metrics... error rate falling, cursor errors dropping to baseline within 90s. Good.
paul (release-lead): good quick mitigation. Can we confirm that the server compatibility path is intact and that proxies with older frames will still work for 2.x clients?
mara (release-engineer): yes servers are backward compatible; the issue was clients flipping to v3 prematurely and some proxy route variants not getting the feature toggle. We'll add a guard in the client that reads FF from server on startup rather than compile-time default.
sophie (customer-ops): customers impacted: 5 enterprise customers with active streaming sessions saw transient disconnects (sessions auto-retry). No data loss reported. I've DM'd their CSMs with the brief.
paul (release-lead): severity assessment: P2 (partial degraded experience for small set), incident will be recorded. Postmortem owner: mara. Targeting a short postmortem doc by EOD tomorrow.
jin (oncall-sre): leaving a runbook step: if we see this again, immediate actions: 1) set FF new_cursor_protocol=false 2) rollback canary to 2.9 3) scale canary down to zero traffic for the release. I'll add to the oncall runbook.
paul (release-lead): rolling out hotfix to CI so client 3.0 won't enable v3 without server-side opt-in. Also gating future client releases behind a canary validation that asserts wire-version backwards compatibility.
devops-bot: scheduled job created: deploy-check-wire-version-compat in CI after this incident.
tom (oncall-asia): I'll take the overnight handoff. Jin, any outstanding tasks for the night?
jin (oncall-sre): monitor the alert group until cleared, validate canary metrics stay at baseline, confirm postmortem draft. If any regression spike >5% over 5m, escalate to paul.
tom (oncall-asia): on it. Taking channel. :thumbsup: 
paul (release-lead): thanks everyone. Mara - feel free to post the final timeline and impact in the ticket and link the postmortem.
mara (release-engineer): will do. Saving logs + commands used in the incident channel. Postmortem TODOs: root cause (client default flip), short-term mitigation (FF kill + rollback), medium-term fix (server opt-in check + client guard), owners assigned.
incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) at 22:22:30 UTC — postmortem expected.
